name: authz: permissions come from roles at every tier; anchor scope is reach, not authority
why: docs/spec/permissions-from-roles.md (owner 2026-09-13): the anchor-tier short-circuit in the permission gate is withdrawn. Pins the two callers it used to let through — a provisioned application service account (anchor-scoped, holding only platform:application-service) reading an admin resource, and an anchor user holding only platform:viewer performing a write — and that reach is untouched: the viewer still reads every client. Java-first: Go keeps the bypass until it mirrors, so the two refusals are allow-listed against Go's 200/201 with the ruling.

steps.why: platform:application-service grants event create and event-type view/create — never IAM reads. Java 403 PERMISSION_REQUIRED; Go's anchor bypass answers 200.
scope ANCHOR needs an anchor-domain email; example.com is the bootstrap admin's own domain (parity-harness.md §2).
reach is untouched: an anchor viewer lists every client (platform:admin:client:view is in platform:viewer).

authority is not: platform:viewer has no event-type create (the event-type routes gate on requireAny(create, update, delete) BEFORE reading the body). Java 403 PERMISSION_REQUIRED; Go's anchor bypass reaches validation and answers 400 on the empty code — deliberately invalid so the bypassed write leaves no event type behind on Go for later scenarios to list. Not /api/clients: that aggregate is gated on anchor reach alone with no permission check on either side — a separate finding.

leave nothing behind: the service-account and event-type lists later scenarios pin are ordered by keys the two sides tie-break differently, and a new row between existing ones exposes that (docs/backlog.md).
